title: I Posted the RC-Track Heat Hours After They Took My Numbered Transponder

parts.text: I stepped into lane two at 11:08 a.m. and marshal Kit was already using my numbered transponder. The board said: ONE HEAT. EIGHT MINUTES. TRANSPONDERS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-three, club marshal, holding a clipboard that listed our heat. Kit shrugged. "Marshals are the heat." I photographed the board, the booking, and his car on my transponder. Then I asked for the heat hours. At 11:12 the track desk pinged why Kit's car sat on our transponder. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The track desk can see Kit's car on lane two during our heat.

social.video_title: He took my numbered RC transponder — Part 1/2
social.description: RC track, a marshal on my transponder, an eight-minute clock he posted. I logged the car. Would you have asked for the heat hours?

parts.text: Kit called it practice laps until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the lane still. The transponder went back to my numbered clip. Kit ran a slot of their own and told the next marshal atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MARSHALS ARE NOT THE HEAT. I keep our heat on a labeled card. Kit brown-bags his cars. The lane finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Heat hours, numbered transponder, and a second line on the board. Were practice laps ever our heat?
